question.text: How many of Brazil's 27 state capitals will the InfoGripe bulletin of 12 November 2026 list at alert, risk or high-risk level with a rising long-term SRAG trend?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the count of state capitals that the InfoGripe bulletin released on Thursday 12 November 2026 lists as being at "alerta", "risco" or "alto risco" SRAG activity level with a growth signal in the long-term trend ("sinal de crescimento na tendência de longo prazo"). The count is the number of capitals named in that bulletin's capital-level ("capitais") statement of how many of the 27 capitals meet this condition; for example, the bulletin released on 29 October 2026 (epidemiological week 42) named 5 capitals (Aracaju, Belém, Cuiabá, João Pessoa, Rio de Janeiro), so that edition would resolve as 5. The source is that edition's "Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe" PDF, expected at https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf (Fiocruz names these files Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_<epidemiological week>.pdf; the 12 November edition is expected to cover epidemiological week 44, 1–7 November 2026). Capitals listed at alert level or above without a growth signal are excluded — in the 29 October edition these were Brasília and Florianópolis.
question.fine_print: If the bulletin is released later than 12 November 2026, resolution uses that first bulletin released after 12 November 2026 that analyses data through 7 November 2026. If the expected PDF is unavailable (e.g. a different file name or suffix), the count is taken from the same edition of the bulletin as published by Fiocruz elsewhere or as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). State capitals are the capitals of Brazil's 26 states plus Brasília (Distrito Federal) — the 27 "capitais" tracked by InfoGripe.

research:
The edition that decides this question (SE 44, due 12 Nov 2026) has not come out yet, so nothing is settled. The last confirmed count is 5 capitals (SE 42). In recent weeks the count has swung between 0 and 5.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: I could not read the PDF text directly. I fetched the SE 42 PDF (8.2 MB), but the tool returned only binary streams, so the figures below come from Fiocruz's news release and the question text. [SE 42 PDF](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_42.pdf)
- 2026-10-29 (SE 42, 18-24 Oct): **5 capitals** at alert or above with long-term growth:
  - Aracaju: young children
  - Belém: ages 2-4 and 50-64
  - Cuiabá: young children
  - João Pessoa: ages 50-64
  - Rio de Janeiro: under 2 and ages 15-49
  - Brasília and Florianópolis were at alert or above without growth. [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/10/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de)
- 2026-10-29: State level: 5 states had growth.
  - Mato Grosso: SARS-CoV-2
  - Mato Grosso do Sul: rhinovirus plus SARS-CoV-2
  - Sergipe: metapneumovirus
  - Maranhão and Amapá: not enough lab data to name a virus
  - Roraima and Santa Catarina were at alert without growth.
  - Nationally, the short-term trend (3 weeks) was rising, while the long-term trend (6 weeks) was stable or oscillating. [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/10/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de)
- 2026-11-02: The SE 43 PDF (Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_43.pdf) returns HTTP 404. It is due on 5 Nov. The SE 44 file is not out yet either. [SE 43 URL](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_43.pdf)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The 12 Nov bulletin covers 1-7 Nov, and some of that week is still to come.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-29: SARS-CoV-2 severe cases rose slightly nationwide, with increases noted in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, but levels are still very low. Metapneumovirus is falling nationally but rising in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Bahia, Pernambuco and Sergipe. Rhinovirus made up 53.3% of positive cases and is stable. [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/10/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de)
- About 2026-10-19 (SE 41 coverage): covid growth signal limited to Mato Grosso. [Afya](https://portal.afya.com.br/infectologia/srag-no-brasil-mantem-estabilidade-mas-sergipe-segue-em-alerta)
- 2026-10-15/16 (SE 40): national SRAG stable or oscillating. Sergipe was the only state at alert with growth. Metapneumovirus was rising in 9 states. [Afya](https://portal.afya.com.br/infectologia/srag-no-brasil-mantem-estabilidade-mas-sergipe-segue-em-alerta)
- About 2026-10-08/09: rhinovirus, metapneumovirus and SARS-CoV-2 were rising, mainly among ages 2-14. Covid was up slightly in 5 states. [Afya](https://portal.afya.com.br/saude/infogripe-identifica-aumento-de-srag-em-criancas-e-adolescentes); [Acessa/Agência Brasil](https://www.acessa.com/noticias/2026/10/341916-virus-respiratorios-ainda-estao-em-alta-no-pais-alerta-fiocruz.html)
- 2026-11-01/02: The news items you collected (storms in the South and Southeast, drought and smoke in Amazonas affecting Manaus, dengue in the Federal District) contain nothing about SRAG. Smoke in Manaus could in principle affect respiratory admissions, but I found no evidence of that.

### 4. Base rates
- Recent series (capitals at alert or above with growth), from the question text:

| Week | Count |
|---|---|
| SE 38 | 3 |
| SE 39 | 5 |
| SE 40 | 0 |
| SE 41 | 5 |
| SE 42 | 5 |

  - Mean is 3.6, median 5. Week-to-week changes have been +2, −5, +5, 0.
  - Membership turns over a lot: only Aracaju, Cuiabá, João Pessoa and Rio de Janeiro carried over from SE 41 to SE 42, and Belém was new.
- Earlier in 2026, per a search-tool summary of the Fiocruz PDFs that I could not check myself:
  - SE 19 (peak season): 16 capitals
  - SE 29: 2 capitals with growth, 12 without
  - [SE 19](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_19.pdf), [SE 29](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_29.pdf)
- Capitals at alert or above without growth have numbered 2 to 6 recently, so the pool that could flip into the count is small. In SE 42 the total at alert or above was 7.
- I could not find the 2025 SE 43-45 capital counts for a same-season comparison.
- Caveat: SE 44 data will be the newest week and subject to reporting delay (nowcast), which adds noise to the six-week trend.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets you collected relate to InfoGripe or SRAG; they cover Brazilian inflation, the election, the central bank, and so on. I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05 (Thu): The SE 43 bulletin (data through 31 Oct) comes out after forecasts close on 3 Nov, but it would be the main guide to which capitals are likely to stay in or join the count. Capitals to watch:
  - The five already in the count
  - Brasília and Florianópolis (at alert without growth)
  - Capitals in states with growth: Campo Grande, São Luís, Macapá
- 2026-11-12 (Thu): The SE 44 bulletin, which decides the question. [Expected URL](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf)
- Ongoing drivers: slight covid rises (Mato Grosso, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo), metapneumovirus in the Northeast and Southeast, and rhinovirus among children.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Cold fronts and severe storm alerts cover Santa Catarina (3 to 5 Nov), Paraná, São Paulo and Mato Grosso do Sul. Cooler weather in the South could matter for respiratory activity, but that link is speculative. Florianópolis is already at alert level without growth. [NDmais](https://ndmais.com.br/tempo/frente-fria-coloca-189-cidades-sob-perigo-de-tempestades-granizo-e-chuva-de-ate-200-mm-durante-a-semana-em-sc/)

This could plausibly affect respiratory admissions, but I found no InfoGripe evidence that it has. [Portal do Holanda](https://www.portaldoholanda.com.br/amazonas/seca-e-fumaca-estado-contabiliza-47-municipios-em-emergencia-e-piora-na-qualidade-do-ar)
- 2026-10-29 (SE 42) findings:
  - States at alert or above with growth: Amapá, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Sergipe and Maranhão.
  - Metapneumovirus is falling nationally but rising in SP, RJ, BA, PE and SE, where it is driving the increase in young children.
  - Rhinovirus is stable nationally and is driving the increase in MS.
  - SARS-CoV-2 rose slightly nationally, with growth in MT, MS, SP and RJ, though at low incidence. It is the main driver in MT.
  - Nationally, SRAG has been stable or oscillating over 6 weeks but rising over the last 3 weeks. That short-term rise could feed into more long-term growth signals.
  
  [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/10/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de)
- 2026-10-15 (SE 40): "Apenas Sergipe" had alert-level SRAG with an upward trend, and no capital qualified. [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/15/infogripe-apenas-sergipe-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-e-tendencia-de-aumento/)

- Membership is persistent but rotates:

  - Rio de Janeiro appears in 3 of 5.
  - Cuiabá and João Pessoa appear in the last two.
- Capitals at alert or above without growth have numbered 2 to 6 per edition. That is the pool that could flip into the count.

Historical highs are far above the current range, for example 18 to 19 of 27 capitals in mid-2022 (SE 25 and 27). - Things to watch:

  - Whether metapneumovirus keeps growing in RJ, SE, PE and BA, which could keep Rio, Aracaju and João Pessoa in the count.
  - Whether SARS-CoV-2 keeps growing in MT, MS and SP, which matters for Cuiabá and could add Campo Grande or São Paulo if they reach alert level.
  - Smoke in Manaus.
  - Brasília and Florianópolis gaining a growth signal.
- 2026-11-02: The All Souls' Day (Finados) holiday may delay data entry into SIVEP-Gripe. That could affect nowcasting of the most recent weeks, but I don't know of any documented effect.
